items.summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.

items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
items.title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

items.summary: The onset of ferromagnetic order in one dimension reflects a competition between domain energy and entropy. For Ising chains with arbitrary translation-invariant, nonnegative, summable pair interactions, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for an ordered phase at positive temperature: the energy required to reverse an interval of N spins must be bounded below by a positive multiple of ln N for all sufficiently large N. When this energy is also bounded above by a finite multiple of ln N, we prove a quantitative magnetization gap, implying a nonzero spontaneous magnetization at the critical temperature and a discontinuous onset of order. No monotonicity, regular decay, or nearest-neighbor coupling is required. The results include sparse and irregular interactions for which r^2 J(r) is unbounded. Our results extend the magnetization jump beyond pointwise inverse-square bounds to every chain whose domain energy has logarithmic upper and lower bounds.
items.title: Onset of Ferromagnetic Order in Ising Chains

The Architectural Shift: From State Catalogs to Relational Compilation A foundational problem across discrete mathematics, quantum simulation, and macromolecular physics is distinguishing between a static state catalog and an executable transformation architecture. Conventional computational models treat physical configurations as external data structures submitted to an independent processor: conformations are enumerated in an address table, transitions are assigned by ad hoc hopping matrices or stochastic Monte Carlo rules, and empirical parameters are fitted post hoc to bulk observables. While effective for descriptive curve-fitting, that paradigm divorces the representation of a state from the lawful operations that generate and invert it. Whenever a coarse observation projects away an internal degree of freedom, a state-only model mistakes an observational quotient or a scheduling collision for an absolute physical barrier. The research program consolidated in this report—spanning the native binary partner rings, the One Inverter twisted clock, the Way Between three-dimensional conformational compiler, and the tetrahedral diamond-lattice and polyethylene matter readers through §167—establishes a rigorous alternative: compilation is the continuing resolution of local relational constraints, and physical observables are typed readouts of the resulting operator algebra. Rather than postulating an external machine or assigning arbitrary binary labels to particles, the architecture begins with the minimal condition for a distinction to persist without terminal fixed points ( ) and traces the exact algebraic and geometric structures forced at each scale. This progression unfolds across four interconnected operational tiers that preserve an explicit way home at every scale by pairing a quotient difference reader with a retained frame or phase coordinate. In the first tier, the native binary ring and twisted clock establish divided left and right representative hemispheres and forward/reverse faces governed by fixed-point-free involutions. In the second tier, the planar honeycomb route compiler lifts into a three-dimensional control torus where synchronous bond torsions execute a diagonal bypass around blocked planar corners. In the third tier, three-dimensional tetrahedral chains on the diamond lattice form an unbranched two-sheeted mirror quotient across a central reflection plane. items.summary: Background/Objectives : With the advent of the current digital health age, opportunities for interacting with health systems have grown not only more frequent but also variable in type, spanning across emergent care settings, routine outpatient follow-up, as well as at-home telemedicine-based platforms. In light of initiatives to re-design electronic medical records (EMR) to more meaningfully curate evidence-based insights, our research objective is focused on harnessing underutilized data features (i.e., time-ordered events) to map the complex interactions that patients undergo within their health systems. We posit that inclusion of information associated with sequential patterns will help more accurately simulate care pathways and outcomes. We report preliminary data on care utilization patterns among cohorts of patients diagnosed with chronic disease. Methods : De-identified data were extracted from the MedStar Health AIM-AHEAD Data Bridge (AADB)’s Chronic Disease repository. EMRs were queried for patients with confirmed diagnoses for diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E10.X or E11.X) as well as heart failure (ICD-10: I50.X). For each unique patient, encounters related to care utilization were sequentially collated, with explicit demarcation of whether interactions occurred before or after corresponding diagnoses. For analytical purposes, encounters were categorized as “Emergency”, “Inpatient”, “Observation”, “Outpatient”, “Home Health”, and “Patient Portal”. For each cohort, sequential pattern mining (SPM) was used to generate antecedent-consequent prediction rules and calculate the conditional probabilities (confidence) of subsequent care utilization episodes. Analyses were performed using R (The R Foundation for Statistical Computing; version 4.5.2). Results : Between January 2018 and December 2024, we distinctly identified 202,605 patients with a diagnosis for diabetes mellitus as well as 79,223 patients with a diagnosis for heart failure. Across both cohorts, 42,208 patients had documentation of being diagnosed with both conditions and were flagged separately for potential sensitivity analyses. The proportion of older patients (50 years or above) was predominant (>85% for all patients). SPM algorithms were used to generate rulebooks associating unique care utilization patterns with their corresponding likelihood of subsequent events. The evaluated methods are: Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Bayesian Information Criterion (PELT-BIC), Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Akaike Information Criterion (PELT-AIC), Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (BOCD), Cumulative Sum control charts (CUSUM), Moving-average ±3σ control-chart baseline. The repository contains the complete workflow used to: verify field records and ground-truth leak timings; perform campaign-specific spectral analyses using multitaper estimation; evaluate changepoint-detection performance; quantify event-level leak detectability; compare observed performance against chance-level expectations; assess BOCD sensitivity to hazard-rate and threshold settings; generate precision-recall curves and average-precision statistics; perform cross-campaign validation analyses; estimate theoretical detection-delay bounds for flow-based detection. This version supersedes earlier releases by correcting changepoint-index alignment, revising false-alarm-rate calculations using exposure time outside detection windows, replacing pooled spectral analyses with campaign-specific multitaper analyses, and incorporating event-level detectability, chance-level benchmarking, precision-recall evaluation, cross-campaign validation, and theoretical detection-delay analyses. Classical acupuncture, Chinese medical philosophy, yin-yang, Five Phases and Daoist thought are welcomed as inherited cultural frameworks capable of generating questions. Established physical laws and metrological statistics likewise remain inherited knowledge rather than purported discoveries by 33 x STARLI. The project does not exclude established scientific knowledge or ancient philosophy; it simply does not include other authors' DOI records in this particular bibliography.

items.summary: Coordinating molecular, cellular, and macroscopic explanations is a core requirement of secondary biology and chemistry, yet classroom assessments still infer a student's developmental level from written answers collected after an inquiry task ends. Digital process telemetry—the timestamped record of a student's clicks, slider sweeps, pauses, and revisions inside a simulation—captures how learners navigate across scales in real time, but raw interaction counts lack a shared unit of measurement with curriculum learning progressions. This study addresses that measurement gap through a two-part validation. First, a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 86 studies (312 effect sizes; 48,920 learners) synthesized cross-scale inquiry interventions and yielded a pooled Hedges' g of 0.642, demonstrating that adaptive next-step scaffolding, paste-guarded response entry, and explicit cross-scale representations each significantly amplify learning gains. Second, using a fixed-parameter reconstruction of that empirical benchmark alongside a simulated bilingual cohort of 1,240 secondary learners and 1,000 Monte Carlo replications, we calibrated six non-intrusive behavioural trace indicators against a 12-item ordered multiple-choice progression bank on a unified Rasch partial credit logit scale. Common-scale linking error was 0.118 logits (10.9% of the critical Level 2–3 transition interval). Trace-based classifications reproduced item-based progression levels with 81.45% accuracy and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient of .768, exhibited strict measurement invariance across language tracks, gender, and prior achievement, and confirmed that genuine self-regulatory behaviours rather than interface guardrails drive diagnostic classification. Behavioural traces can thus provide calibrated, equitable coordinates for real-time formative support in secondary science classrooms.
items.title: From Clicks to Constructs: Event-Stream Process Mining, TreeSHAP Attribution, and Rasch Partial Credit Calibration of Behavioural Trace Indicators for Cross-Scale Science Reasoning

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach
